subject: scenario-viola-run-start-sequence-to-child-spawn
origin: ## 4. Span / Trace Coverage › #### Scenario: `viola run` start sequence to child spawn
text: - **Must-trace spans:** `run.start` (INTERNAL, root) › `run.collision_check` › `run.pin_copy` › `run.conpty_sideload` (Windows) › `run.version_gate` (spawns the `version-probe`) › `channel.bind` › `run.budget_eval` (INTERNAL, `trigger="start"`; its attributes are under Scenario: Budget governor; chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor) › `state.snapshot_write` › `state.heartbeat_start` › `pty.spawn` (CLIENT). Two start steps carry no span and no log line, by design (the operator's answer at the chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through wrap; that chunk's plan added no span name): the statusline source read, whose result is the snapshot's `statusline_command`, and the settings override write (`instances/<name>/settings.json` through `replace_private`, Unix only), which sits between the first snapshot and `pty.spawn`. The child's `--settings` argument, the source path and the command appear in no line or span. A third start step carries none either, as landed (chunk 2026-10-10-session-links): the link set's restore, one read pass over the instance's `events.ndjson` through `viola_state::events::read_from`, made beside the wait feed's rebuild and before the endpoint serves. It appends nothing and logs nothing, its result is the first snapshot's `links`, and the start appends no record for links, so the span chain above and the product order below are unchanged; `viola revive` starts through the same function.

origin: ## 4. Span / Trace Coverage › #### Scenario: `viola run` start sequence to child spawn
text:
- **Required log fields:**
  - Common fields with `process="run"` and `corr` null.
  - `process-start{subject:"self", service_name, version, os, pid, endpoint_kind}`.
  - `process-start` / `process-exit{subject:"version-probe", child_exit_status, duration_ms}`.
  - On failure, `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail}` with `detail` ∈ `already-live|squatted-name|pinned-hash-mismatch|batch-script-child` (Founder Direction 4; no path or pid). `viola revive` enters the same sequence through the same start, after an instance check that precedes the log init and writes no line when it refuses, then a preflight of its own whose refusals add `detail` ∈ `no-session|session-live|cwd-missing` (and `already-live`, from the same collision check) before any child is started; its `session-live` reading (skipped under `--fork`) writes one `process-start` / `process-exit{subject:"agents-probe"}` pair in `run-<name>.ndjson`, plus one `parse-rejected{parser:"claude-agents-json"}` on an oversize or malformed answer, and passes on a failed read; a revive that passes its preflight runs `run.collision_check` twice, once in the preflight and once inside the start.
  - On success, `process-start{subject:"claude-child", child_pid, pty_backend, cli_version, cli_verified, env_stripped_count, env_stripped_known, env_kept}` (D-34), plus, on Windows when the `run.conpty_sideload` outcome is not `loaded`, `sideload_fallback` (`hash-mismatch|unreadable|load-failed|not-built`, D-36). A degraded sideload adds no `process-exit{exit_code:1}` and no panic line.
  - In `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, `pty_backend` is `{ "type": "string" }`, while `sideload_fallback` is closed in the `process-start` properties to `hash-mismatch|unreadable|load-failed|not-built` (`diag-detail.v1.json` carries neither). A sideload degrade is recorded on the existing info-level lines, never at `warn`, and no companion path or hash reaches a home-level line (D-36).
  - Product order `wheel{cause:"start"}` → `budget-gate` → `session-start` is verified from `events.ndjson` through `agent-run logs --kind`, not duplicated into process logs (`run` writes the first two; `session-start{source:"hook"}` is record three, sent by `viola hook` through `hook.event` since "Hooks to normalised events"; the harness `boot` readiness stage `start_records` checks `events.ndjson` lines 1-3 — `wheel{cause:"start"}` → `budget-gate` → `session-start{source:"hook"}` — with the missing code `<name>:events`).

subject: log-details
text:
- `process-exit` exit 1: `already-live` (a `live` or a `stale` holder of the name, from `viola run` or from `viola revive`, which prints `run`'s own collision pair, or under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"already-live","detail":null}` document — revive's preflight refusals under `--json` are the same-shaped document with their code, the logged line unchanged (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract); a `gone` holder is taken over with no exit-1 line), `squatted-name`, `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `batch-script-child`, `internal-error`, and from `viola revive`'s start-arm preflight `no-session` (no logged session, or an `--id` the log does not hold), `session-live` (one `claude agents --json` read lists the logged session id live in another `claude`; skipped under `--fork`; a failed, oversize or malformed read passes, fail open; chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) and `cwd-missing` (the snapshot records no directory, or one that is not an existing directory). The preflight reads the holder, then the session, then `session-live`, then the directory, and takes no later reading once one refuses; each refusal is one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail}` in `run-<name>.ndjson` with no child started. `strict-modes-failed` is no longer one of them (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor): the start arm's instance check (`check_instance`) runs before the wrapper log opens and outside the preflight, so its refusal is the stderr `unable:` / `hint:` pair (or under `--json` the `strict-modes-failed` document, chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract) and exit 1 with no log opened, no `process-start`, no `process-exit` and no child.
 And `interrupted`: a `viola verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (Unix `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`, Windows Ctrl-C / Ctrl-Break) before its rows are checked ends with one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}` in `cli-<name>.ndjson` under a `VIOLA_NAME` (no file with no instance, D-06), after every spawn pair it opened is closed (chunk 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup). `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` closes the `process-exit` `detail` at 13 values (the enum's members; 12 before chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, 11 before chunk 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup, 9 before chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive).

subject: log-details
text: - Refusal details are the arch `RefusalReason` details verbatim: `manual-pause`, `five-hour`, `seven-day`, `input-not-ready`, `no-prompt-submitted`, `turn-running`, `unknown-dialog`, `control-character`, `empty-text` (an empty typed text on `send`; it adds no field, and `send-refused.detail` is an open string in `diag-line.v1.json`).

subject: errors
text: - vt100 panics are caught on `run`'s feed thread (`src/run/gate.rs`) by a `catch_unwind` around each feed and resize, not inside `run.readiness_gate`. Each poisoning episode gives exactly one `parse-rejected{parser:"vt100-feed", count:1}` at `WARN` with no `corr`, its `detail` set by the cause: `panicked` for a caught vt100 panic, `oversize` for a copy the bounded feed queue dropped (a size message carries the drop count at its offer, so a drop after a queued resize poisons the fresh screen again). The model stays poisoned until the host size changes, and `run` continues. `viola_panic_hook` runs before the catch returns, so a panic poisoning also writes the hook's `event:"panic"` role line and its detail line. Witnessed at run level by `tests/chaos_feed_panic.rs` (chunk 2026-10-04-confirmed-send-with-cl-1-records): exactly one `parse-rejected{vt100-feed, panicked}` and one `event:"panic"` line, both asserted present, then `viola send` refused `send-refused{detail:"input-not-ready"}` (exit 13) while a typed key still reaches the child. G2's single seam exemption is unchanged: that test's home lives outside `target/e2e-home` (`TestHome::outside_scan()`), so G2, G4 and the secret scan do not read it (the founder's ruling, live, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer).
